paper.title_en: Multiple Andreev Reflection Spectroscopy of Spin-Resolved Proximity States
paper.abstract_en: We study coherent multiple Andreev reflections (MAR) in short constrictions connecting superconductor-ferromagnet bilayers with parallel exchange fields. Proximity-induced spectral reconstruction produces split and redistributed differential-resistance anomalies, modifying both odd- and even-order subharmonic features, unlike a rigid Zeeman shift of BCS spectra. The shifted anomalies are approximately governed by the interval between the parent superconducting gap edge and an exchange-dependent spectral singularity. Qualitative spectral-interval estimates for antiparallel alignment are given in the Supplemental Material. Channel-transparency averaging extends the description from short ballistic constrictions to short diffusive multichannel junctions, where the characteristic anomalies survive. These findings provide a route to probing spin-resolved proximity states through two-terminal charge transport.
